texts: The net is full of worldly catch and the throat still dry; only the Name's water can end this ache.
doha about a net of pleasures and a soul still parched for God

I have been caught in a net of pleasures and gains for years, yet my throat stays parched for something none of them gives. Please write a doha about this aching thirst for God that nothing worldly can quench.
My uncle has everything the world offers, trapped in his net of deals, but at night he sits silent and says something inside is still dry.
parched in a net
sandalwood, stone, parched soul
Sandalwood cools the brow, the stone gives rest, yet the throat of the soul stays dry till the Lord is tasted.
I rub sandalwood on my forehead and sit on a flat stone at dusk, but nothing settles this restless dry feeling for the Divine.
Sandalwood paste cools the skin and a smooth stone offers shade to sit on, but the dryness inside me goes on; compose a doha about a spiritual thirst that no cooling comfort of this world can quench.
doha with sandalwood and a stone about longing for God that nothing cools
doha: a priest and a mountain cannot quench the soul's craving for God
The priest's chanting fills the air, the mountain is climbed, and the throat of the soul is still dry.
I went up the mountain with my family and the priest gave us blessings, but I came down still feeling this strange dry hunger for God.
priest, mountain, dry soul

The priest recites for hours and the mountain pilgrims climb with bleeding feet, yet my heart is still dry and aching for the divine, so please write a doha about that unquenched craving beyond rituals.
However much I pour from the pot of water, the dryness in my heart does not end, because what I crave is not water but the Lord; compose a long doha on this ache that nothing worldly quenches.
The pot of water empties and refills, yet the soul's dry throat waits for another, deeper drink.
pot of water, parched heart
doha about a pot of water and a soul craving God more than water
My mother keeps a pot of water by the bed and says she is thirsting for something no water will ever quench, something close to God.
I wandered the market for hours looking for I do not know what, and a musk deer toy seller laughed that I was searching in the wrong place.
market, musk deer, craving
In the crowded market I looked for relief and a musk deer ran past carrying his own scent, and I realised my craving for the Divine would never be met by anything on sale; write a doha for me.
The market sells all things and the musk deer runs mad for what he carries; the soul's craving is met nowhere outside.
doha with a market and a musk deer about the soul's craving for God
After a good life and a full table I still wake some nights with a strange emptiness that feels like needing something holy.
a doha for when nothing worldly satisfies and you crave God like a dry throat
I drink and eat and the whole world pours into me, yet something inside stays dry and begs for God; please write a doha capturing this craving in the heart that no earthly cup has ever filled.
The world gives and gives, yet the soul stays dry; only the Beloved's name will quench it.
the dry soul
just give me a doha about an aching need for God that nothing satisfies
Summers in our village the ground splits open, and lately I feel like that ground, waiting for something that I cannot name.
cracked earth, parched soul
The summer earth cracks open to the sky, and so does the soul that has heard the Name and tasted nothing yet.

O how my soul craves a single taste of the Divine, parched as dry earth in the summer, while streams of worldly pleasure run past without ever cooling it; please write a doha for this deep spiritual need.
jaggery cannot satisfy
doha with jaggery about sweetness of the world not satisfying a craving for God
The jaggery is sweet on the palate yet the throat of the soul stays parched; it craves only the Lord's name.
Jaggery is sweet and so is success, but neither touches the dry ache for the Divine in my chest; compose a doha for the spiritual thirst that no sweetness of the world can ever satisfy.
I ate the best jaggery sweet at my promotion party and still felt something dry inside, as if I needed a different kind of sweetness.
Pot of water full and the net pulled in, yet the throat is dry; what the soul wants is not in the world's catch.
I carry a pot of water to the pond and watch the fishermen's net come up full, and I wonder why my own hunger for God never ends.
doha with a pot of water and a net about a thirst for God nothing quenches
pot of water, net, parched
I filled the pot of water and cast a net into the pond of the world, hoping to catch contentment, but my throat is still parched for something I cannot name; write a doha for that craving for God.
My grandmother sifts grain with a winnowing fan and mends with thread, and says all her labor leaves the same dry ache for God in her chest.
doha with a winnowing fan and a thread, a soul parched for the Divine
The winnowing fan sifts the husk, the thread mends the cloth, but nothing mends the soul's dry craving for the Lord.
With a winnowing fan I separated the grain and with a single thread I mended my shawl, but I cannot mend the dryness of my longing for the Divine; compose a doha on that.
winnowing fan, thread, dry soul
My tongue is so dry that it clings to the roof of my mouth, and the peacock crying in the courtyard sounds like my own heart begging for the Divine; please write a doha about this inner craving.
dry tongue, peacock cry
doha with a dry tongue and a peacock crying for rain, craving the Divine
The peacock cries to the sky, my tongue clings dry; both of us crave a drink no earth can pour.
When the peacock screamed at dusk my tongue stuck to my mouth, and I realised it was the sound of what I felt for God.
river, yet dry
I live on the banks of a great river, and still some mornings I wake with a dry craving that I know is for something holy.
The river flows beside me, the throat is dry; it is not this water the soul is craving.
The river runs full right beside me, and still I stand on the bank with a dry throat, because what I crave is not water at all but the Lord; write a long doha about this ache.
doha about standing by a river and still parched for God
doha with a water well and an oil press, a soul parched for God
water well, oil press
Our water well is full all year and the oil press never stops, but my mother still sits on the steps at night craving something more.

Water well deep and cool, the oil press turning in the shade, and yet I stand with a parched throat longing for the Divine; compose a doha on the soul's dry craving that nothing in the world can satisfy.
The water well is deep, the oil press creaks, but the soul's dry throat is not eased by anything the village holds.
Nothing the earth offers can wet the lips of the soul; it waits for the one drop that is the Lord.
Please write a doha about a longing of the soul that is like severe thirst, a dry craving for the Divine that no earthly water, fame or pleasure has ever been able to wet even for a moment.
the soul's dry craving
doha for a soul that aches for God like a dry throat for water
I have everything people dream of and somehow I wake at night with my mouth dry as if I need something holy.
The pot of water fills me for an hour and leaves me dry by evening, for the soul needs the Lord's drink.
doha: a pot of water cannot quench the soul's craving for the Lord
Each pot of water I drink from leaves me dry again, because what I crave is not the water but the Lord; write a doha about this deep spiritual need that no vessel of the world can fill, please.
I keep emptying one pot of water after another on summer afternoons, and it reminds me that my craving for God is a dryness water cannot fix.
pot of water, dry
The moneylender counts his pearls, the night comes, and his throat is dry for what no pearl can buy.
moneylender, pearls, parched
My uncle, a moneylender with a casket of pearls, told me once that all his wealth cannot wet the dryness he feels in his chest at night.
doha about a moneylender and pearls who still crave the Divine
The moneylender counts his pearls and thinks he owns the world, yet at night his throat is dry with a craving no riches can answer; please compose a doha on the soul's thirst for God.
Soft cotton cannot cool the parched soul; only the Beloved's name moistens such a throat.
cotton bed, dry soul
Cotton soft as down lines my bed, yet I toss all night with a dry ache for the Divine that no comfort in the world can soothe; write a doha in which this craving rises like a plea.
I have the softest cotton mattress in the village and still cannot sleep, my chest dry with some craving I cannot name.
doha with soft cotton and a restless dry soul craving God
cremation ground, still craving
At the cremation ground I saw all appetite burn out, and still the craving for something beyond the world stayed with me, dry and strong; compose a doha about that deepest thirst.
doha about a cremation ground and a craving for the divine that outlasts it
After the cremation of my father I felt every wish go dry in me except one, the strange need for God.
The cremation ground burns every appetite, yet the soul's dry craving walks away from the pyre still alive.
doha about a traveler parched in the desert as the soul craves God
traveler with parched lips
A traveler trudges across a burning desert with a cracked mouth, thinking only of water, and I thought that is how the soul craves the Divine; write me a doha on this inner parching.
A traveler stopped at our gate begging for water, and as I gave it I felt that I too have been walking and craving something for years.
The traveler walks the dry road dreaming of water; the soul walks the world dreaming of the Lord.
Spinning wheel and grindstone keep turning, and the soul stays dry; only the Lord's name is the moisture it craves.
doha with a spinning wheel and a grindstone, the soul craving the Divine
The spinning wheel turns all day and the grindstone grinds the grain, yet my work leaves a dry ache for the Divine which no labor of the hands can satisfy; write a long doha about it.
spinning wheel, grindstone, dry soul
Grandmother spins at her spinning wheel and grinds at the grindstone from dawn, and says it is all a way to forget she is craving God.
doha with a lotus and a mosque about a soul still craving God
The lotus drinks the pond and I drink prayers at the mosque, yet my throat of the soul is dry.
I pray at the mosque every Friday and admire the lotus pond outside, yet the dryness inside me for the Divine doesn't ease.
lotus and mosque, still dry
The lotus blooms in water and still I stand dry at the mosque, craving a drink that rituals do not give; compose a doha about the longing of a soul for God that prayer alone cannot slake.
doha about the soul's craving for God that nothing earthly satisfies
Life has been good to me, so I do not understand why my heart feels so dry, like it is waiting for something sacred.
Nothing in the world is enough; the soul craves a single drink that does not run out.
dry, craving, God
So many comforts and yet this endless dryness inside, a craving that has no name except God; can you write a doha capturing the thirst of the spirit that nothing in life can satisfy, please?
doha with a churn and a lock, the soul still craving God
My aunt churns butter and keeps a lock on the chest, but she told me nothing in that chest can wet the dryness she feels for God.
churn, lock, craving
I turn the churn all morning and keep a lock on my treasure chest, yet nothing quenches the dry longing in my soul; write a doha about this aching thirst that neither work nor wealth can end.
The churn turns, the lock holds the treasure, and the throat is dry; the soul wants the Lord, not butter.
a doha on the craving for God that no water or food can fix
There are nights when a plain dry feeling rises in me, a craving for the sacred so strong that no food or drink can touch it; please write a doha about the soul parched for the Divine.
parched land, parched soul
Some nights I wake with my throat dry and know it is not water I need, it is a kind of prayer.
The soul is a dry land that no worldly rain can wake; only the Lord's grace is the monsoon it craves.
A moneylender in our town gave away half his silver last year and said no amount of it ever wet the dryness inside him.
The moneylender's chests are full, his soul is a dry hollow, and he craves one drop of the Lord.
moneylender, dry soul
doha about a rich moneylender with a dry soul craving God
The moneylender has silver in every chest and still wakes in the night with a dry mouth and a hunger for God that his wealth cannot reach; compose a doha about that ache of the soul.
Every dish at my table, from bitter gourd to fresh butter from the churn, leaves me wanting the one taste that is divine.
doha with a bitter gourd and a churn, tasting everything but craving God
The bitter gourd is bitter and the churn spins butter, but neither the sour nor the sweet flavors of this life quench the craving of my soul for the Divine; write a doha for me, long and quiet.
bitter gourd, churn, craving
Bitter gourd and churned butter, every flavor of life I have tasted, and still the throat of the soul is dry.
just a doha for the craving of the soul that nothing the world gives can fix
Everyone around me is satisfied after the rains but I still feel a dryness that, I think, can only be answered by God.
The fields drink the monsoon, the soul drinks the world, and both end up dry in the heat of the Lord's absence.
Rain falls on the fields and the fields drink, but my soul stays dry; please write me a doha about the longing of a heart for the Divine that has drunk everything else the world had to give.
the dry heart
I tried yoga, travel, new jobs, nothing satisfies this thing in me that I think is just a need for God.
A thousand pleasures pass by the lips and the soul stays dry, for the Lord's name is the only water for it.
a thousand pleasures, still dry
doha: thousands of cups and the soul still dry, craving the Divine
If a thousand cups were handed to me I would still be dry, because the thing I crave is the Divine, not a drink at all; write a doha for this ache that cannot be wet with any worldly water.
My mother sat at the spinning wheel all through my childhood, and I now see she was perhaps trying to forget a dry craving for God.
The spinning wheel turns the day to cloth, but the throat of the soul is dry and wants the Lord's drink.
doha with a spinning wheel and a soul's craving for the Divine
The spinning wheel hums and my mind should be quiet, but my soul feels a dry craving for the Divine that spinning does not ease; compose a doha about the ache that work cannot soothe.
spinning wheel, craving
Years of working hard and travelling, and I still feel like a dry twig waiting for rain, and I suspect the rain is divine.
a doha on a dry soul and a craving for God nothing worldly can end
parched soul
The dry soul longs for the Lord as a dry land for rain; nothing less than His grace will wet it.
My soul is dry as a twig left in the heat, and no water, wealth or worship has moistened it; can you compose a long doha about this deep craving for God that has no worldly cure?
My wife wears a pearl necklace that was meant to make her happy, but she sits at the window at night with a parched, wanting look.
The merchant sells pearls from far seas and the buyer drinks the finest wine, but my soul is dry and no pearl can wet it; compose a doha on the craving of the soul for the Divine.
pearl cannot quench
doha with a pearl, the soul still parched for the Divine
The pearl is bright and the wine is rich, yet the throat of the soul is dry, begging for the Lord.
doha: a moneylender with a full cup but a parched heart craving God
The moneylender's table is full, his cup is full, his heart is a dry bed that waits for one drop of the Lord.
The moneylender has bags of coin, a rich table and a full cup, and yet his heart is a dry riverbed; write me a doha on the aching craving for God that no wealth has ever quenched.
Our village moneylender sits alone every evening with a full cup in his hand and a face like he needs some other kind of water.
moneylender with a dry heart
Watching a moth circle the glow and the rainbird call outside, I felt that both of them express my craving for the divine better than I do.
The moth circles a bright light and the rainbird opens her beak to the sky, both desperate for what they cannot reach, and so is my soul in its craving for God; please write a doha on this.
The moth wheels for the glow, the rainbird waits for the drop, and the soul cries out for its Lord.
doha with a moth and a rainbird both craving what they cannot reach, like the soul
moth, rainbird, craving
door and lotus, still dry
When I opened the door that morning the lotus was in bloom on the pond, and I felt a pang of dryness, like I was missing something sacred.
I opened the door and saw a lotus on the pond, so perfect that I wept, because even the flower drinks and I do not; write a doha on the soul's dry craving for the Divine.
doha with an open door and a lotus, craving God while the flower drinks
At the open door a lotus floats upon the pond, drinking its fill, and the soul stands dry and watching.
doha for a soul that craves one drop of the divine
Everything is fine in my life but there's this nagging dryness and I think it's just my soul asking for God.
My lips are dry and my mind is quiet, and I know the thing I crave is not of this world; will you write a doha about the soul longing for a single sip from God?
One sip from the Lord and the soul would never be dry again; until then the lips keep asking.
a sip from God
The blind man asks the physician for water and receives herbs; the soul's craving needs the Lord and none else.
blind man, physician, dry soul
doha with a blind man and a physician about the soul's dry craving for God
My blind uncle went to the physician for a dry cough, and what he really wanted, he told me later, was to feel close to God.
A blind man stumbles to the physician with a dry throat and the physician offers him herbs, yet what he craves is the Lord whom neither can see; compose a doha about the soul's aching dryness.
Standing at a crossroads near the ocean, I realised no road would lead to the one thing my heart is dry for.
doha with an ocean and a crossroads, the soul craving what the world cannot give
The ocean is bitter and the crossroads confuses, but the soul is dry for the sweet water of the Lord.
ocean, crossroads, dry soul
At the crossroads of life I stood by the ocean of worldly choice, drinking everything and yet dry in my heart; please write a doha about the soul craving only the Divine.
a doha for someone who tried everything and still craves God

Not wealth, not fame, not friends, not feasts: nothing wets the lips of my spirit, which is parched for God; compose a doha for a heart that has tasted everything the world offers and craves only the Divine.
I got the promotion, the car, the flat, and still my mouth is dry in the middle of the night for something I cannot buy.
beyond worldly pleasures
The pleasures of the world are all tasted and set down, and the soul still asks, in its dry voice, for the Lord.
doha: dry field waiting for rain, a soul waiting for God
My father stood in the dry field this summer staring up at the sky, and I recognized that look from my own craving for God.
waiting for rain
Like a dry field waiting for the first monsoon rain, my soul sits waiting for one drop of the Divine; please write a long doha about the craving that nothing in the world has been able to settle.
The land waits, the sky is silent, the soul stays dry; one drop of grace would wake it green.
blind man and dew
doha with a blind man and the morning dew about craving the Divine
A blind man at the shrine steps was catching dew in his palm at dawn, and said it was a poor substitute for what he really craves.
The blind man sits by the roadside licking the morning dew from the grass, craving more than dew can give, and so my soul craves the Divine; write me a long doha on this.
A blind man licks the dew and still is dry; the soul sips the world and is dry until the Lord pours.
the one thing
The world has every pleasure but one, and that one is the Lord; the soul will take no other.
I have noticed that no meal or holiday fixes the dry feeling, and I think I need God more than I knew.
doha on a soul that is parched and wants only God
It is not water or food or sleep that I need but a deeper drink from the Divine, and I feel it every hour; write a doha for the soul parched in a world that offers everything but that.
I planted a seed during the drought and it just sat there dry, and I thought: that is me waiting for something from God.
A seed lies dry in the soil waiting for the rain, and so does my soul lie waiting for a drop of the Divine; compose a long, gentle doha about that dry craving the world cannot quench.
doha with a seed in dry ground, a soul craving the divine drop
a seed waiting for rain
The seed in the dry earth waits for rain, and the soul in the dry world waits for the Lord's drop.
doha about the soul being parched and needing God more than anything
A lifetime of drinking and the lips still dry; the soul remembers a spring it cannot find.
I get up every morning with a dry feeling that coffee doesn't fix, and I think it is a kind of prayer I haven't said.
forever dry
What I need most is not rest nor food but a drink of the Divine, and I have been parched for it forever; please write a doha for the long craving that nothing in this world can end.
We drove to the ocean and then up the mountain, and with all that beauty I still felt something dry that I knew was only for God.
Standing beside the vast ocean I felt my craving for the Divine more than ever, and a mountain in the distance seemed to call, but neither could wet the dry throat of my soul; write a doha.
doha with an ocean and a mountain, a soul craving more than scenery
ocean and mountain, still dry
The ocean is vast and the mountain tall, but the throat of the soul is dry; neither one is the Lord.
A lotus opens each dawn to drink the morning, and I too open to the Divine each day but remain dry; please write a long doha about a soul that cannot be wet by anything but God.
lotus drinks, soul stays dry
doha with a lotus that drinks the dawn, while the soul stays dry for God
The lotus drinks the dawn and opens, but the soul opens daily to a sky that does not rain the Lord.
I watched a lotus open in the pond this morning and thought, why can't my own soul drink like that and be satisfied?
A thorn has torn my foot and I am walking the road with a dry mouth, yet what I crave is not rest but the Lord himself; compose a doha about that craving no worldly comfort answers.
A thorn in the foot, dust in the throat, and the soul walks on dry, with only one word in its heart: the Lord.
I had a thorn in my foot the whole pilgrimage and a dry mouth, and none of that mattered next to the craving for God.
doha with a thorn and a dry throat, the soul walking to the Lord
thorn and dry throat
All my worldly comforts have turned to ash in my mouth, and what is left is a dry, plain craving for the Divine; write me a doha for the soul parched beyond all remedy of the world.
ash in the mouth
The comforts turn to ash and the throat of the soul stays dry; the Lord alone is the cure.
After my big plans burned down to ash I realised what I was craving all along was a presence I cannot explain.
doha: worldly comforts turned to ash, only a craving for God remains
Please, a doha: my soul is a dry earthen cup waiting for the Lord to fill it, and nothing the world pours into it ever stays; I long for the Divine with a thirst I cannot name.
doha: the soul as an empty cup waiting for the Lord
an empty soul
The soul is empty and the world pours in, and it is empty still; only the Lord's hand fills it.
There is a dryness in me that no weekend or holiday fixes, and I think maybe it is God that I am missing.
My uncle runs an oil press and my aunt runs a churn, and they both say their labor leaves a dryness only God can touch.
Oil is pressed and butter churned, and the soul is as dry as before; only the Lord's name is its drink.
doha with an oil press and a churn, a soul craving the Divine beyond work
oil press and churn
The oil press squeezes out the day and the churn whirls the cream, but nothing I make from the world's labor wets the dry craving of the soul for the Divine; compose a long doha on it.
The diamond glitters on the palace floor and the king drinks from a silver cup, yet his throat is dry for a drink he can neither buy nor command; write me a doha about the soul's craving for God.
I visited a palace with a diamond on display, and a guard told me even the king had told his advisers that he was still empty.
diamond, palace, parched king
doha with a diamond and a palace, a king still craving the Divine
The diamond shines in the palace and the king's cup is full, yet the soul within him is dry for the Lord.
